name: the per-table count is read from the live table only
why: THE trap org/503-handling.org names for this design. runFilter() REMOVES non-matching rows, so a live-DOM tally collapses toward zero as rows are filtered out — and a control that hides itself at zero then vanishes exactly when a filter excludes the rows it is the only way back to. CLAUDE.md records the identical bug for _updateLengthMismatchButtons() and _updateLiveDateFlagButtons().

name: every per-table control shows the page-wide count
why: A control rendered per table but carrying the page-wide number would pass any 'the controls exist' check while partitioning nothing. The sum assertion is what distinguishes them.

name: entity paths are not deduped within a table
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden. A sticky-column duplicate of a row carries the same art anchor, and a release-group breadcrumb can repeat one, so a tally that counts occurrences rather than distinct paths over-reports. A Set is used, and swapping it for an array would show the defect — but this fixture has no repeated art anchor within one table, so the sum assertion still holds. Covering it needs a fixture with a sticky column over an artwork column.

name: the Relationships done-set is partitioned instead of page-wide
why: KNOWN GAP, recorded rather than hidden. The same entity can appear in several tables and _relWriteResult() clears the error marker only on the cells it writes, so an MBID answered in table A must not still count as failed in table B — which is why the done set accumulates across every table before any subtraction. This spec disables the Relationships column (its ws/2 traffic is unrouted here), so the Rel half is exercised only indirectly, by the rel specs in the suite calling the refresh on every pass. Covering it needs a multi-table fixture with a repeated entity and routed ws/2.

edits.replace: _entries.forEach(e => { const d = new Set(); d.forEach(m => e.mbids.delete(m)); });
